title: Distinct gut and lung microbiota profiles in a naturally occurring equine model of asthma
description: Feces, plasma and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were collected from six horses with severe equine asthma in exacerbation and six healthy control horses housed in the same barn and fed the same dry hay diet. Bacterial communities in feces and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were characterized by sequencing the V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene, and short-chain fatty acid and lactate concentrations were quantified by chromatography in all three compartments. Technical control specimens were sequenced alongside the low-biomass airway samples to identify probable reagent contaminants. The study compared fecal and lung community membership, structure and alpha diversity between groups, and examined paired cross-compartment relationships within individual horses.
